newsitem.title: DUBAI: HORSE RACING-RAIN THREATENS DUBAI WORLD CUP.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-RAIN THREATENS DUBAI WORLD CUP.

text.p: A sudden downpour has threatened the cancellation of Saturday's Dubai World Cup, the world's richest horse race, the organisers said.
Host Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum decided to cancel the first four races of the six-race meeting in the interest of safety, race committee spokesman Brough Scott said.
The two big races of the day, including the $4 million Dubai World Cup, were under review following the downpour on the sand track.
He said the paramount criterion in reaching a decision was the well-being of the 13 horses and jockeys chasing the $2.4 million winner's prize. "That will be number one," Scott said.
The Dubai World Cup was due to be run at 8.15 p.m. (1615 GMT).
